title: A Panel Data Analysis of Determinants of Financial Inclusion in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) Countries from 1999 to 2024
decision_rationale: Empirical panel regression where internet users (internet diffusion) is a regressor for financial inclusion (family 5); the paper states 45 SSA countries (Table 5 uses 34 cross-sections), above the 10-economy minimum. Internet is one of several determinants rather than the sole focus, so inclusion is borderline.
exposure_measure: USERS: number of internet users (WDI; descriptive mean 11.183, likely per 100 people but unit not stated); also SERVER: secure internet servers

sample.income_groups_covered: not reported (SSA, mainly low and lower-middle)

design.estimator: Panel least squares, pooled regression (no fixed effects reported)
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: GDP per capita, inflation, interest rate, Islamic banking dummy, money supply, credit; no country or time effects reported

results.indicator: Financial inclusion (AFII; depositors with commercial banks per 1000 adults) on internet users
Financial inclusion on secure internet servers

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language ('enhance') with pooled OLS, no fixed effects or instruments; reverse causation and omitted variables unaddressed. Durbin-Watson 0.12 indicates strong residual autocorrelation.

exposure_measurement.why: Internet users unit not defined; secure servers is a weak proxy and is negative.

selection_of_countries_years.why: 45 countries stated but 34 cross-sections and 598 unbalanced obs used; unexplained.

outcome_measurement.why: Outcome defined as depositors per 1000 adults in text but labelled AFII in table; mean 21.4 inconsistent with scale of some regressors; inconsistent reporting.

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: Unit root tests run but pooled levels regression estimated anyway; no fixed effects despite stated need for panel methods; R-squared line garbled (1436).

selective_reporting.why: Only one specification reported, so little room to judge.

venue_quality_concern: possible (MDPI journal; internal inconsistencies in tables and variable definitions)
notes: Abstract mentions Panel Least Squares and three periods (pre-COVID, COVID, post-COVID) but no period-specific results reported. Table 5 reports pooled results only, though the text says panel methods are needed. Table 2/3 headers use GRO for GDP per capita and ISIC/ISMAIC inconsistently. No instruction-like text found.
